correctness.rationale: P=product Delta(c_i,q_i) and H=Delta(R,N). For a H-vertex selecting j_i coordinates in block i, Euclidean projection retains chosen ones and redistributes missing rank equally if j<=c, or scales selected ones if j>=c. Supporting-normal optimality gives squared gap phi_i(j). Each piecewise phi is C1 and strictly convex over [0,q_i], so a two-coordinate +/-1 occupancy transfer strictly improves at least one way whenever two blocks are partially occupied. Thus all vertex maximizers have at most one partial block, yielding the candidate max. On balanced (q,c)=(2a,a), all block phi<=a/2 strictly below inside: equality R/2 exactly when equal-sum PARTITION subset exists. The projection-residual strict Jensen inequality forces all continuous equality points to be the distinct full/empty binary H vertices. Binary-encoded block parameters provide polynomial reduction and NP witness, giving weak rather than strong NP-completeness. Independent check: Wrote a separate Fraction-based exhaustive occupancy enumerator for four heterogeneous profiles ((2,4,6),(1,2,3)), ((2,6,8),(1,3,4)), ((2,3,5),(1,2,2)), ((3,5,8),(1,3,2)). Exact maxima were 3,4,109/30,24/5; every maximizer has at most one partial block. Verified supporting-normal projection condition analytically and the equal-sum PARTITION equivalence, without treating cases as an infinite proof.
residual_risks: Weak NP-completeness pertains only to succinct binary block-size/rank descriptions; explicit ambient N-coordinate representation has different input length.
